scheme_name: Scholarship to the Ward of Beneficiary (CBOCWWB)
description:
The Scholarship to the Ward of Beneficiary scheme is a welfare initiative launched by the Government of India.

This scheme is specifically designed for the children of construction workers who are registered with the Construction Workers Welfare Board.

The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to the wards of registered construction workers for their education.

It was initiated to ensure that the children of laborers do not face barriers in accessing quality education due to financial constraints.

The scheme was launched in 2006 under the Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1996.

The primary objective of the scheme is to promote education among the children of construction workers.

The scheme aims to provide scholarships to students from Class 1 to post-graduation levels.

The scholarship amount varies based on the educational level of the student.

For students in Class 1 to Class 5, the scholarship amount is ₹1,000 per annum.

For students in Class 6 to Class 8, the scholarship amount is ₹2,000 per annum.

For students in Class 9 to Class 10, the scholarship amount is ₹3,000 per annum.

For students in Class 11 to Class 12, the scholarship amount is ₹5,000 per annum.

For students pursuing undergraduate courses, the scholarship amount is ₹10,000 per annum.

For students pursuing postgraduate courses, the scholarship amount is ₹15,000 per annum.

The scheme also aims to encourage higher education among the wards of construction workers.

To be eligible for the scholarship, the applicant must be a child of a registered construction worker.

The construction worker must be registered with the respective State Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

The applicant must be studying in a recognized educational institution.

There are no specific age limits mentioned for eligibility.

However, the applicant must meet the educational criteria for the respective scholarship amount.

The income of the construction worker must not exceed ₹15,000 per month.

The application process for the scholarship is straightforward.

The applicant must fill out the application form available on the official website of the respective State Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

The application form must be accompanied by specific documents.

These documents include a copy of the construction worker's registration certificate.

A copy of the student's admission proof in the educational institution is also required.

The applicant must provide a copy of the income certificate of the construction worker.

The application must also include a passport-sized photograph of the student.

Once the application is complete, it should be submitted to the local office of the State Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

The application is then reviewed by the concerned authorities.

The scholarship is usually disbursed annually.

The disbursement is made directly to the bank account of the beneficiary.

The scholarship amount is credited within a few months of the application approval.

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Labour and Employment.

Each state has its own Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

These boards are responsible for the implementation of the scheme at the state level.

The contact details for the respective State Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board can be found on the official website of the Ministry of Labour and Employment.

The scheme has been instrumental in supporting the education of many children of construction workers.

As of 2023, it is estimated that over 1 million children have benefited from this scholarship scheme.

The scheme has played a significant role in reducing dropout rates among children of construction workers.

The scholarship has also contributed to improving literacy rates in communities with a high concentration of construction workers.

The government has allocated a budget of ₹500 crores for the welfare of construction workers in the financial year 2023-2024.

This allocation includes funds for the Scholarship to the Ward of Beneficiary scheme.

The scholarship is a part of the broader initiative to enhance the welfare of construction workers and their families.

The scheme is regularly monitored and evaluated to ensure its effectiveness.

Feedback from beneficiaries is taken into account to improve the scheme.

The government encourages construction workers to register with the welfare board to avail of the benefits.

Awareness campaigns are conducted to inform workers about the scheme and its benefits.

The scheme is aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals, particularly Goal 4, which aims to ensure inclusive and equitable quality education.

The scholarship is a crucial step towards achieving educational equity for marginalized communities.

The scheme has received positive feedback from various stakeholders, including NGOs and educational institutions.

The government aims to expand the reach of the scheme to cover more beneficiaries in the coming years.

Efforts are being made to streamline the application process for better accessibility.

The scholarship is a testament to the government's commitment to supporting the education of underprivileged children.

The scheme is a vital resource for families struggling to afford educational expenses.

It empowers children to pursue their academic dreams without the burden of financial constraints.

The government continues to seek innovative ways to enhance the effectiveness of the scheme.

Overall, the Scholarship to the Ward of Beneficiary scheme is a significant initiative that reflects the government's dedication to improving the lives of construction workers and their families.
